hayden.dt: Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden introduced himself as a blacksmith from Rosenau. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
One of the first hundred, Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden was given the First Wave ribbon. He wrapped the accompanying paper against the damp.
After what happened at the Brickworks, Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden asked to serve as a field cook. Nobody argued.
A crow sat on the parapet above Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden all afternoon. The men say it chose him.

Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden tried to dry a page near the stove. The paper survived, but the message now has the smell of toasted bread. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
Karel Check and Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At the change of watch, the next pair was told it had been a good hour.

A shell landed square in R-F10. They found Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. The shell that hit R-F10 took Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden with it. No stretcher, no surgeon, no last words. Just the crater.

Pavel "Crow" Hayden asked about Isidor "Rabbit" Hayden on arriving at R-F10. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. Pavel "Crow" Hayden answered the first call, number 73 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
